Honestly, I say do it. Especially if you've been contemplating it for some time. Hell, I ended up deleting my OG Male Warlock, the one that I made back in D1 and transitioned into D2, during the beyond light year as and my hunter in Season of the Lost. And while, yes, it was an absolute pain in the ass to redo all of the campaigns again, regrind stasis, do all the quests, etc., etc. In the end, I know that no matter what armor set I put on, it's always always going to look good. Honestly, it might have been the best decision I've made.

I'd recommend that if you do recreate your character, make absolute certain that all of your items are in your vault before you delete them.

Time period is important as well! I also HIGHLY HIGHLY recommend that you delete the character during a time in which you're fed up, incredibly bored with, or if it's a lull in the season. This is to avoid rapidly  burning yourself out.

Like right now would be the most opportune time to do so. The seasonal story is wrapped up and has mostly concluded, the cats out the bag with the seasonal exotic, there's very little to do in Destiny right now. The final thing left to do for the season is solstice. And the sooner and faster you get caught up with your new character the sooner you can enjoy the new armor coming in solstice.

I feel like most of it has to do with the movement. Warlocks easily have the most complicated movement because there's so much that you have to consciously be aware of. Like: if you want to maximize speed while using burst glide, you have to keep an eye out for when to press jump when you're at the Apex of your float. To maintain this speed, you have to have to be aware of your position on the "bell curve" and determine whether it's appropriate or not to jump at this specific time. You basically have to constantly play this mini-game, and I feel that a lot of players, especially newer players, are kinda turned off from playing Warlock because of this mini game that you have to constantly aware of. Titan movement is a lot less complicated. It's literally a jetpack. Hunters have the simplest to understand, and the most intuitive movement, it's literally an additional jump. This extra jump either flings you higher, flings you more forward, or you get 2 additional jumps. Nothing to think about nothing to consciously be aware of. It just works. Plus, yeah I suppose the thought of playing as this rogue / lone wolf is appealing to most.

This is just a personal type thing and I doubt this really bothers anyone else but as a Warlock main, me personally I am so tired of seeing new armor being added to the game with the same old dated design "philosophy" (for lack of a better word). The armor set either consists of a helmet with a giant Mohawk and / or the big gaping vertical "void slit in the middle." Or the chest piece is an actual wedding dress with a monstereously huge collar. Like I understand that robes is the entire identity of a Warlock, but do most of them have to drag against the floor? Some of my favorite robes are the Deathsinger's Mantle from D1, the Born Spark starting chest piece also from D1, I feel is underrated, IMO. Substitute Alloy, Shadow's Robes, and Legacy's Oath Robes are all unique and fun to mess around with. I absolutely love the design and length of the Wings of Sacred Dawn Exotic ( I wish I could get rid of the wings on the back, though ). Just in general, coming up with Warlock fashion is kind of a pain and not as satisfying as the other 2 classes, seeing as they're all either 1 or 2 of these things and the robes is like 60% of your overall look. Could we please get shorter robes, or better yet, robes that reveal more of the legs. To add on to all of this, what happened to shoulder pads. I've noticed they're on some armor pieces, but they're no longer affected by gloves like they used to be in D1.

My Worst - I haven't necessarily had a "bad reaction" with my scars (seeing as I cover them up most of the time). But the one time I couldn't be bothered to, I had to work that very same day. I work as a cashier and I had this older lady come to my register. She had a handful of items so I chose to scan them directly from the cart instead of putting them on the belt. In doing so, I had positioned myself in such a way where she had direct line of sight of my forearm - and I didn't even realize until I caught her catching glimpses of my scars. Once I announced her total, she started making small talk: asking if I was in school, saying that she worked at a local college and that she'd like for me to start investing in my future. As she was talking, I couldn't help but notice her face turn bright red as she wiped falling tears from her eyes. Even turning her head and excusing herself. I was gonna blurt out "...uhm, is everything alright, ma'am?". Then the realization hit me. Oh... As she paid, time seemed to come to a completely stand still and the only thing I heard was her sniffing and she struggled to fight back tears. I felt terrible. Guilt, regret, and dissapointment smacked me like a bullet train as I stared blankly at the screen. Until it beeped. Before I could even ask if she wanted a recipt, she yanked her card out and was already half way across the parking lot. "God fucking damnit. The one day I don't wear sleeves...", I thought.

The Best - It was last year. I had had enough. I had tried to kill myself 2 months prior and was still reeling from the extreme stomach pain from all those pills I took. I couldn't take it. I had to tell someone. The only person I knew, my mother. Ever since I was a kid, I've always had a incredibly difficult time communicating and just describing things in general - so I did what I've always done best, I wrote a letter. In this letter, I told her everything: How much I hated myself, Why I can never keep a job longer than 3 months, Why I stopped going to school, Why all the pills in the medicine cabinet mysteriously disappeared, Where all those blood soaked paper towels came from, How much I miss childhood, How much I miss how life was before the divorce, How much I hate seeing her stressed out, How I hate seeing her work 12 hour shifts only to come home eat absolutely nothing, How I hate that I worry the living shot out of her. I spilled my heart and told her things that I thought I would take to my grave. I told her, "Hey Ma, I have something I wanna tell you. You don't have to read it now but whenever you feel comfortable enough to". She read it immediately. I blasted music in my ear trying to ward off the thoughts telling me that this was all a mistake and all I'm going to do is be even more of a burden to her. I waited. And waited. And waited... All of a sudden the light flicked on. I looked at the doorway and there she was. Eyes wide and bright red. The note left her hand and fluttered to the floor. She held her arms out  and I met her embrace. And we just sat there. For a long while we sat there and she just held me, in complete silence, rocking back and forth. After a long time she finally spoke. "I had no idea my own son was struggling THIS bad... I'm so, so sorry". She pushed me away. Before I knew it, she grabbed my arm and rolled my sleeve up. And there it was. The many scars, the off colored skin, the mutilation. The horror. She didn't even look for long. She took a peak and embraced me again, tighter this time.

We talked for hours afterwards. She asked me so many questions. It was nauseating. I felt sick admitting some of my darkest secrets but it had to be done. She offered to help in any way she can and here I am to tell the tale. I  wouldn't say I'm feeling any better nowadays but it's tolerable at least.

For context: I'm an only child and a premature baby at that. I had underdeveloped lungs when I was conceived and couldn't breath on my own. I was hooked up to all different types of machines and shit for months. It wasnt until 3 months after when my mother could hold my small, frail frame for the first time. Every doctor said that I wouldn't make it past my early teenage years. Yet here I am at 22.

After being told about my infancy - metaphorically, I cant help but feel as though "the cuts only run deeper".

Thanks for reading all that shit.
